ABC Islands.label: the ABC Islands
ABC Islands.intro: Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao lie off the coast of Venezuela, south of the hurricane belt, so they are dry, sunny and breezy all year — the safest Caribbean choice in hurricane season. The winter months are the busiest and most expensive; late spring and early autumn are calm, hot and good value.
seasons: December–April
High season: dry, breezy and the busiest time, with Carnival in February or March.
May–September
Hot, calm and quieter, with the clearest water for diving.
October–December
The short rainy season: brief showers, but still mostly sunny.

Alaska.intro: Alaska's travel season is short: from late May to mid-September, when days are long, wildlife is active, cruise ships sail the Inside Passage and Denali's park road is open. June and July have the most daylight and the best weather; August is wetter but brings salmon runs and bears feeding at rivers. Winter is dark and very cold, but it's the season for the Northern Lights.
seasons: June–August
Peak season: long days, open parks, cruises and wildlife — book early.
May & September
Shoulder months: quieter and cheaper, with some lodges and tours closed.
October–April
Cold and dark, with the Northern Lights, dog sledding and skiing.

Alps.label: the Alps
Alps.intro: The Alps have two peak seasons: winter skiing from December to April and summer hiking from late June to September, when cable cars, mountain huts and high passes are open. Late spring and late autumn are quiet in-between seasons when many lifts and hotels close.
seasons: Late June–September
Summer: hiking, lakes and Alpine flowers; mountain huts and high passes open.
December–April
Ski season, with the most reliable snow from January to March.
May & October–November
In-between seasons: quiet and cheaper, but many lifts, huts and hotels are closed.

Andalusia.intro: Andalusia, in Spain's sunny south, is best in spring and autumn. Seville and Granada are among the hottest cities in Europe in July and August, often topping 40°C, while winter is mild and mostly sunny — with snow on the Sierra Nevada above Granada.
seasons: March–May
Spring: warm days, orange blossom, Holy Week and Seville's April Fair.
June–September
Hot: inland cities often reach 40°C, so plan early starts and siestas.
October–February
Mild and sunny with some rain; skiing in the Sierra Nevada from December.

Argentina.intro: Argentina stretches from subtropical Iguazu to sub-Antarctic Patagonia, so the best time depends on where you go. Buenos Aires and the wine country shine in spring and autumn, Patagonia is a summer destination, and Bariloche has a ski season from July.
seasons: November–March
Summer: Patagonia's trekking season with long days; hot and humid in Buenos Aires.
March–May
Autumn: grape harvest in Mendoza and mild, golden days in Buenos Aires.
July–September
Winter: skiing in Bariloche; Patagonia is cold and many lodges close.

Arizona.intro: Arizona's low deserts around Phoenix and Scottsdale are a winter-sun destination, while higher places like Sedona and the Grand Canyon's South Rim are best in spring and autumn. Summer is dangerously hot in the desert, and July–September brings monsoon thunderstorms. The Grand Canyon's North Rim is open only from mid-May to mid-October.
seasons: March–May
The best all-round time: warm in the desert, mild at Sedona and the Grand Canyon.
June–September
Extreme heat in Phoenix; afternoon monsoon storms from July.
October–February
Ideal desert weather in Phoenix and Scottsdale; cold and sometimes snowy at the Grand Canyon.

Australia.intro: Australia is huge, and its seasons are the reverse of the northern hemisphere's. The tropical north (Cairns, the Great Barrier Reef) is best in the dry winter, while Sydney and Melbourne shine in spring and autumn.
seasons: September–November
Spring: warm in the south and still dry in the tropics — a great all-round time.
December–February
Summer: beach season in Sydney and Melbourne, but hot, wet and stormy in the far north.
June–August
Winter: the best time for the reef and the north; cool and crisp in the south.

Austria.intro: Austria is a two-season country: summer for Alpine hiking, lakes and festivals, and winter for skiing and Christmas markets. Vienna is best in spring and autumn, when it's mild and the concert season is in full swing.
seasons: May–September
Hiking, lakes and the Salzburg Festival; warm in Vienna.
December–March
Ski season in the Tyrol, plus Christmas markets in Vienna and Salzburg in December.
April & October–November
Quieter shoulder months, with some lifts and mountain huts closed.

Balkans.label: the Balkans
Balkans.intro: The Balkan coast — Croatia, Montenegro and Albania — has hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Late spring and early autumn are ideal, combining warm seas with fewer cruise passengers and lower prices than July and August.
seasons: May–June
Warm, sunny and green, with long days and the sea warming up.
July–August
Peak season: hot and crowded on the coast.
September–October
Warm sea and harvest season, with smaller crowds.

Baltic States.label: the Baltic States
Baltic States.intro: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania have short, bright summers and long, cold winters. From May to September the days are long — almost endless around midsummer, when the region celebrates its biggest festival — and the medieval old towns of Tallinn and Riga are at their best. December brings Christmas markets but only six or seven hours of daylight.
seasons: May–September
Long, mild days, White Nights in June and midsummer festivals.
October–November & March–April
Cool, grey shoulder months with low prices.
December–February
Cold and dark, often below freezing, with Christmas markets in December.

Brazil.intro: Brazil is mostly tropical and warm all year, so the timing is about rain and festivals. Rio and Salvador are hottest in the southern summer around Carnival, the Amazon has high- and low-water seasons, and Iguazu Falls is impressive all year.
seasons: December–March
Summer: beach season and Carnival in Rio and Salvador; hot, with tropical downpours.
April–July
Rainy season in Salvador; high water in the Amazon for canoeing the flooded forest.
August–November
Drier and pleasantly warm in Rio; low water in the Amazon reveals river beaches and trails.

California.intro: California's coast, deserts and mountains have very different seasons. San Francisco is warmest in September–October, Los Angeles and San Diego are sunny most of the year, deserts like Joshua Tree are best in spring and autumn, and the Sierra Nevada has a summer hiking season and a winter ski season.
seasons: March–May
Spring: wildflowers in the desert, waterfalls in Yosemite and green hills.
June–August
Summer: high-country hiking and Lake Tahoe beaches; foggy in San Francisco and very hot inland.
September–November
Autumn: the warmest, clearest weather on the coast and grape harvest in Napa.

Cambodia.intro: Cambodia is tropical, with a dry season from November to April and a rainy season from May to October. November to February is the most comfortable time to explore Angkor; March to May is very hot.
seasons: November–February
Cool, dry season: the best time for Angkor and Phnom Penh.
March–May
Hot season, with temperatures often above 35°C.
June–October
Rainy season: green landscapes, fewer visitors and afternoon downpours.

Canada.intro: Canada's travel season is defined by its winters. Summer opens the Rockies' lakes and trails, autumn brings spectacular colours in Quebec, and winter is for skiing and carnivals.
seasons: June–September
Summer: warm days, open mountain roads and ice-free lakes.
Late September–October
Fall colours in Quebec and the east; quieter parks in the west.
December–March
Winter: skiing in Banff and Whistler, Quebec's Winter Carnival — and serious cold.

Canary Islands.label: the Canary Islands
Canary Islands.intro: The Canary Islands lie off the coast of Morocco and have spring-like weather all year, with highs of 21–29°C. Winter is the high season for sun-seekers from northern Europe; summer is hot, dry and breezy. Lanzarote and Fuerteventura are the driest, while Tenerife and Gran Canaria have cloudier, greener north coasts.
seasons: October–April
Winter-sun season: 21–24°C highs, the busiest and priciest time.
May–June & September
Warm and quiet, with the sea at its warmest by September.
July–August
Hot and dry, with strong trade winds and occasional Saharan dust (calima).

Caribbean.label: the Caribbean
Caribbean.intro: The Caribbean is warm all year, so the best time to go depends on rain and hurricanes. The dry high season runs from December to April; hurricane season lasts from June to November, peaking from August to October — though islands like Aruba and Curaçao lie south of the hurricane belt.
seasons: December–April
High season: dry, sunny and breezy — and the most expensive time to go.
May–July
Shoulder season: hot, with occasional showers, lower prices and few storms.
August–October
Peak hurricane season: the cheapest time, best for Aruba and Curaçao.

Central America.intro: Central America has a dry season ('summer') from about December to April and a green, rainy season from May to November. The Caribbean coast often follows a different pattern, with drier weather in September and October.
seasons: December–April
Dry season: sunny beaches, easy travel and the highest prices.
May–August
Green season: morning sun, afternoon showers and lower prices.
September–November
The wettest months on the Pacific side; hurricane risk on the Caribbean coast.

Central Europe.intro: Central Europe has warm summers and cold, grey winters. Spring and early autumn are ideal for city breaks in Prague, Vienna, Budapest and Kraków, summer brings festivals and lakes, and Advent turns the region into Christmas-market heaven.
seasons: April–June
Mild weather, blossoming parks and manageable crowds.
July–August
Warm to hot, with festivals, river terraces and lakes — and peak crowds in Prague.
Late November–December
Christmas markets in every city; cold but festive.

Chile.intro: Chile is over 4,000 km long, from the Atacama Desert in the north to Patagonia in the south. The desert is good year-round, Santiago and the wine valleys are best in spring and autumn, and Torres del Paine is a summer-only trek.
seasons: November–March
Summer: the season for Torres del Paine and Patagonia, and warm days in Santiago.
March–May & September–November
Spring and autumn: mild in Santiago and the wine valleys; ideal in the Atacama.
June–September
Winter: ski season in the Andes near Santiago; Patagonia is cold and quiet.

China.intro: China is vast, with hot, wet summers and cold, dry winters in much of the east. Spring and autumn are the best times for Beijing, Shanghai and Xi'an; Yunnan in the southwest is mild year-round. Avoid national holidays, when the whole country travels.
seasons: April–May
Spring: mild, mostly dry weather for the Great Wall and cities.
September–October
Autumn: the classic best season, with clear skies — but avoid Golden Week (1–7 October).
June–August
Summer: hot and humid with heavy rain in the east and south; plum-rain season in June.

Colombia.intro: Colombia sits near the equator, so temperatures barely change through the year; altitude and rainfall make the difference. Medellín is spring-like all year, while Cartagena is hot and best in the dry season.
seasons: December–March
The main dry season across most of the country, and the busiest time on the Caribbean coast.
June–August
A shorter dry spell in the Andes; Medellín's flower festival in August.
April–May & October–November
The wettest months, with afternoon downpours.

Costa Rica.intro: Costa Rica has a dry season (verano) from December to April and a green season the rest of the year. The Pacific side — Guanacaste and Manuel Antonio — follows this pattern, while the Caribbean coast is often driest in September–October.
seasons: December–April
Dry season: sunny beaches and easy wildlife spotting, but the highest prices.
May–August
Green season: lush forests, morning sunshine and afternoon showers, with lower prices.
September–October
The wettest months on the Pacific side — but the best time for the Caribbean coast.

Croatia.intro: Croatia's Adriatic coast is a classic summer destination, but the shoulder seasons are its sweet spot: warm sea, sunshine and far fewer crowds in Split and Dubrovnik.
seasons: May–June
Warm, sunny and green, with long days and fewer cruise passengers.
July–August
Peak season: hot weather, the warmest sea and the biggest crowds.
September–October
Still-warm sea and harvest season — many travellers' favourite time.

East Africa.intro: East Africa — Kenya and Tanzania — has two dry seasons that line up perfectly for safaris, mountain climbs and beaches: the long dry season from June to October, when the Great Migration crosses the Mara River, and a shorter one from late December to February.
seasons: June–October
Long dry season: prime safari time, river crossings, Kilimanjaro climbs and Zanzibar’s best beach weather.
December–February
Short dry season: calving in the southern Serengeti and hot, sunny beach days.
April–May
Long rains: some camps and island hotels close, but the parks are green and empty.

Eastern Europe.intro: Eastern Europe has warm summers and cold winters, so late spring and early autumn are the sweet spots for city breaks in Prague, Budapest, Kraków and Tallinn, while the Adriatic coast and Albania are best from June to September. Winter brings Christmas markets and low prices but short, freezing days in the north.
seasons: May–June & September
Warm, sunny days for cities and lakes, with fewer crowds than midsummer.
July–August
Hot and busy on the coast; the best time for the Baltic and the beaches.
November–March
Cold, often below freezing, but cheap — and festive in December.

Ecuador.intro: Ecuador sits on the equator, so temperatures barely change; altitude matters more. Quito is spring-like all year, with a dry season in June–September, while the Galápagos has a warm, sunny season and a cooler, drier 'garúa' season with richer marine life.
seasons: June–September
Dry season in the Andes and Quito; cooler, nutrient-rich seas in the Galápagos.
December–May
Warm season in the Galápagos with calm, clear water; wetter in Quito.
October–November
Shoulder months: still mostly dry in Quito, with good value.

Egypt.intro: Egypt is a winter-sun destination. Sightseeing in Cairo and Luxor is most comfortable from October to April, while the Red Sea coast stays warm enough for swimming much of the year.
seasons: October–April
Warm, sunny days ideal for temples, tombs and Nile cruises.
March–May & October–November
Perfect Red Sea weather: hot sun and warm water without extreme heat.
June–August
Intense heat, especially in Luxor and Aswan — sightsee at dawn.

Florida.intro: Florida is warm all year, but its seasons matter. Winter and spring are dry and pleasant; summer is hot and humid with daily thunderstorms, and August to October is peak hurricane season.
seasons: November–April
Dry season: sunny, mild and the most popular time to visit.
May–September
Hot, humid summer with afternoon storms — theme parks are busiest in school holidays.
August–October
Peak hurricane season: keep plans flexible and consider travel insurance.

Florida Gulf Coast.label: the Florida Gulf Coast
Florida Gulf Coast.intro: Florida's Gulf Coast has some of America's whitest sand and calmest water, from Destin and 30A in the Panhandle to Clearwater and Siesta Key near Tampa. Spring is the sweet spot; summer is hot with daily thunderstorms, and hurricane season runs from June to November, peaking from August to October. The Panhandle is noticeably cooler in winter than the Tampa Bay beaches.
seasons: March–May
The best beach weather: warm, dry and sunny, with the Gulf warming up.
June–September
Hot and humid, with afternoon storms and hurricane risk from August.
November–February
Mild and dry; good for walking and golf, though the water is cool.

France.intro: France has a season for everything: Paris is lovely in spring and autumn, Provence and the Riviera shine from May to September, the Alps are a ski destination from December to April, and Alsace's Christmas markets glow in December.
seasons: April–June
Spring: mild weather in Paris, blooming Provence and uncrowded beaches on the Riviera.
July–August
Summer: lavender, festivals and beach season — hot and busy, especially in the south.
December–March
Winter: skiing in Chamonix and the Alps, and Christmas markets in Strasbourg.

French Polynesia.intro: French Polynesia is warm all year. The dry season from May to October brings sunshine, lower humidity and cooler nights, while November to April is hotter and wetter, with occasional cyclones.
seasons: May–October
Dry season: sunny, breezy and the most popular time to visit.
November–April
Wet season: hot, humid and showery, with cyclone risk from January to March.
April & November
Shoulder months: good weather and better rates on overwater bungalows.

Germany.intro: Germany has warm summers and cold, grey winters. Late spring to early autumn is the best time for cities and beer gardens, late September brings Oktoberfest, and Advent (late November to Christmas) is the magical season of Christmas markets.
seasons: May–September
Beer-garden weather, festivals and long days in Berlin and Munich.
Late September–early October
Oktoberfest in Munich — book far ahead.
Late November–December
Christmas markets in every town; cold, but festive.

Greece.intro: Greece's best weather runs from May to October. The islands are at their liveliest in summer, but late spring and early autumn bring warm seas, sunshine and smaller crowds — and on many islands, most hotels close in winter.
seasons: May–June
Warm and sunny, with wildflowers and fewer crowds — ideal for islands and sightseeing.
July–August
Peak season: hot (often 35°C+ in Athens), busy and pricey, with strong meltemi winds in the Cyclades.
September–October
Warm sea, harvest season and thinner crowds — the sweet spot for many travellers.

Greek islands.label: the Greek islands
Greek islands.intro: The Greek islands run on a summer season: most hotels, ferries and tavernas open from about April or May to October. June and September are the sweet spots, with warm seas and fewer crowds than July and August, when the meltemi wind also blows hardest in the Cyclades.
seasons: May–June
Warm and sunny, with the sea warming up and everything open.
July–August
Peak season: hot, crowded and expensive, with strong meltemi winds in the Cyclades.
September–October
Warm sea, softer light and fewer people — many travellers' favourite time.

Hawaii.intro: Hawaii is warm all year, with only a few degrees between seasons. The real differences are rain (more in winter, especially on north and east shores), whales (December to April) and prices, which peak at Christmas and in summer.
seasons: April–June & September–October
The sweet spot: dry, sunny and cheaper, with fewer crowds.
December–March
Winter: whale season and big North Shore surf, but more rain and peak prices.
July–August
Summer: dry and calm seas, busy with family holidays.

India.intro: India is huge, and its weather is shaped by the monsoon. Most of the country — Rajasthan, Goa and Kerala — is best in the dry, sunny winter, while the high Himalaya of Ladakh opens up in summer, when the monsoon soaks the plains.
seasons: October–March
Peak season for Rajasthan, Goa and Kerala: dry, sunny and comfortably warm.
April–June
Pre-monsoon heat on the plains (often 40°C+); a good time for the hills.
June–September
Monsoon rains across most of India; the best time for Ladakh and other rain-shadow regions.

Indian Ocean Islands.label: the Indian Ocean Islands
Indian Ocean Islands.intro: The Indian Ocean islands are warm all year, but each has its own rainy season. The Maldives and Sri Lanka's west coast are best from December to April, Mauritius and Madagascar from May to November, and the Seychelles and Zanzibar in the calm months between the monsoons. Cyclones affect Mauritius and Madagascar from January to March.
seasons: December–April
Dry season in the Maldives, Sri Lanka and the Andamans; cyclone season further south.
May–November
Cooler, drier months in Mauritius, Madagascar and Zanzibar; monsoon rain in the Maldives.
April–May & October–November
Calm seas between the monsoons — the best diving in the Seychelles.

Indonesia.intro: Indonesia straddles the equator, so it's warm all year and the seasons are about rain. Most of the islands travellers visit — Bali, Lombok, Java and Komodo — share a dry season from about April to October and a wet season from November to March.
seasons: April–October
Dry season across Bali, Lombok, Java and Komodo: sunny days, calm seas and the busiest time (July–August).
November–March
Wet season: humid, with heavy afternoon downpours and rougher seas — but greener and cheaper.
April–June & September–October
Shoulder months: mostly dry weather with fewer crowds than midsummer.

Italy.intro: Italy's best seasons are spring and autumn, when it's warm enough for the coast but comfortable for walking around Rome, Florence and Venice. July and August are hot and crowded, and many locals take their holidays in mid-August.
seasons: April–June
Mild to warm, blossoms and long days — great for cities and the countryside.
July–August
Hot and busy, best for the beaches of the Amalfi Coast and Sicily.
September–October
Warm sea, grape harvests and fewer crowds.

Japan.intro: Japan has four distinct seasons. Spring cherry blossoms and autumn leaves are the most popular — and most crowded — times, while summer is hot and humid and winter brings snow to Hokkaido and crisp, sunny days to Tokyo.
seasons: Late March–May
Cherry blossoms and mild weather; Golden Week (late April–early May) is very busy.
June–August
June is the rainy season; July–August is hot, humid and festival-filled. Okinawa has typhoon risk.
October–November
Comfortable temperatures and autumn leaves — many people's favourite time.
December–February
Cold and dry in Tokyo and Kyoto; powder snow and the Snow Festival in Hokkaido.

Kenya.intro: Kenya has two dry seasons that suit both safaris and the coast: the long dry season from July to October, when the Great Migration reaches the Maasai Mara, and a shorter one from late December to February.
seasons: July–October
Great Migration in the Maasai Mara and dry, sunny weather on the coast.
December–February
Hot and dry: good game viewing and the best beach weather in Diani.
April–May
Long rains: some camps close, but the parks are green and empty.

Lowcountry.label: the Lowcountry
Lowcountry.intro: The Lowcountry — the coastal plain of South Carolina and Georgia around Charleston, Savannah and Hilton Head — is best in spring, when azaleas bloom and it's warm but not yet sticky, and in autumn. Summers are hot and humid with afternoon thunderstorms, and hurricane season peaks from August to October. Winters are mild and quiet.
seasons: March–May
The best time: warm days, azaleas and magnolias, and festivals.
June–September
Hot and humid, with storms and hurricane risk from August — beach season on Hilton Head.
October–February
Mild and pleasant in autumn, cool and quiet in winter.

Malaysia.intro: Malaysia is hot and humid all year, with rain arriving at different times on each coast. The west coast — Kuala Lumpur, Penang and Langkawi — is driest from December to February, while Malaysian Borneo is best from March to October.
seasons: December–February
Driest months on the west coast: the best time for Langkawi and Penang.
March–October
Drier season in Sabah (Borneo): ideal for wildlife and climbing Mount Kinabalu.
September–November
Wetter on the west coast, with heavy afternoon storms.

Mediterranean.label: the Mediterranean
Mediterranean.intro: The Mediterranean has hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. June and September are the best months for most beach trips — the sea is warm and the crowds thinner than in July and August — while spring and autumn suit sightseeing. The east (Cyprus, Türkiye, the Greek islands) is warmer and drier than the west.
seasons: June & September
The sweet spot: hot sun, warm sea and fewer crowds.
July–August
Peak season: hottest, busiest and most expensive, with heatwaves inland.
November–March
Mild and green but rainier; many beach resorts and ferries close.

Mexico.intro: Mexico's dry season from November to April is the best time for most of the country, from Cancún's beaches to Mexico City's museums. Summer brings rain and, on both coasts, hurricane risk from August to October.
seasons: November–April
Dry, sunny and warm — peak season on the beaches.
May–June
Hot before the rains; good value in the highlands.
July–October
Rainy season with afternoon storms; hurricane risk on the coasts, especially September.

Middle East.label: the Middle East
Middle East.intro: The Middle East is a winter-sun destination: from November to March, Dubai, Oman, Qatar and Jordan are warm and sunny, while summer brings extreme heat, often above 40°C in the Gulf. Jordan’s Petra and Wadi Rum are best in spring and autumn.
seasons: November–March
Peak season: warm, sunny days and pleasant evenings — ideal for beaches, deserts and city sightseeing.
April–May & October
Hot in the Gulf, but a lovely time for Jordan, with warm days for Petra and Wadi Rum.
June–September
Extreme heat and humidity in the Gulf; low season prices for indoor attractions and resorts.

Morocco.intro: Morocco is a year-round destination with big regional differences. Spring and autumn are ideal for the imperial cities and the desert, the Atlantic coast stays cool in summer, and winter brings snow to the Atlas Mountains.
seasons: March–May
Spring: warm, green and the best all-round time for Marrakech, Fes and the Sahara.
June–August
Hot inland (35–40°C+); breezy and pleasant on the coast at Essaouira.
September–November
Autumn: warm and sunny again, with harvest season and fewer crowds.

Nepal & Bhutan.label: Nepal & Bhutan
Nepal & Bhutan.intro: Nepal and Bhutan share the Himalayan seasons: clear skies and the best mountain views come after the monsoon in October and November, and spring (March–May) brings rhododendrons and warmer days. The June–September monsoon hides the peaks.
seasons: October–November
The classic trekking season: dry, clear and crisp, with festivals like Dashain, Tihar and Bhutan’s tshechus.
March–May
Spring: warmer days and rhododendrons in bloom; some haze over the mountains.
June–September
Monsoon: lush and green but wet, with cloud over the peaks and leeches on the trails.

Netherlands & Belgium.label: the Netherlands & Belgium
Netherlands & Belgium.intro: The Netherlands and Belgium have a mild, changeable maritime climate, with rain spread through the year. Spring brings the famous tulip fields, summer is the warmest time for canals and café terraces, and December has Christmas markets.
seasons: Mid-March–May
Tulip season (peaking in mid-April) and mild weather for Amsterdam and Bruges.
June–September
The warmest, longest days, with outdoor terraces and boat trips.
November–February
Cold, grey and damp — brightened by Christmas markets and lights in December.

New England.intro: New England has four dramatic seasons. Fall foliage from late September to October is the headline act, summer is ideal for the coast of Maine and Massachusetts, and winter brings snow and skiing in Vermont.
seasons: Late September–October
Peak fall foliage, moving from northern Vermont and Maine down to Massachusetts.
June–August
Summer: warm coastal weather, lobster shacks and island hopping.
December–March
Winter: cold and snowy, with skiing in Vermont; many coastal businesses close.

New Zealand.intro: New Zealand's seasons are the reverse of Europe's and North America's. Summer (December to March) is best for hiking and beaches, while winter brings skiing around Queenstown.
seasons: December–March
Summer: warm, long days and the best hiking weather.
March–May
Autumn: settled weather, golden colours and fewer crowds.
June–September
Winter: ski season in Queenstown; cool and wet in Auckland.

Norway.intro: Norway offers two completely different trips: summer's midnight sun, fjords and hiking, or winter's northern lights, snow and dog-sledding above the Arctic Circle.
seasons: June–August
Midnight sun, mild weather and the best time for fjords and hiking.
September–March
Northern lights season in Tromsø and the Arctic.
December–January
Polar night in the north: no sunrise, but magical light and auroras.

Pacific Northwest.label: the Pacific Northwest
Pacific Northwest.intro: The Pacific Northwest is famously rainy — but mostly from October to May. Summers are dry, sunny and mild, making July to September the best time for Seattle, Vancouver, the Olympic Peninsula and the Oregon Coast.
seasons: July–September
Dry, sunny summer: the best weather for hiking, beaches and city trips.
April–June
Spring: blossoms and waterfalls, with showers and cool days.
October–March
The rainy season: grey and wet on the coast, with snow in the mountains.

Patagonia.intro: Patagonia, shared by Argentina and Chile, is a summer destination: from November to March the trekking routes, lodges and boat trips are open and days are long. It is windy all year, especially in summer. Autumn (March–April) brings red beech forests and fewer people; in winter most of the far south closes, but Bariloche becomes a ski resort.
seasons: November–March
Trekking season: long days and the best weather, but strong winds and busy trails.
March–April
Autumn colours and fewer crowds, with shorter, cooler days.
May–September
Winter: many lodges and treks close; skiing in Bariloche.

Peru.intro: Peru's dry season (May to September) is the best time for the Andes, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Lima is the opposite: sunny in summer (December to April) and grey under coastal mist the rest of the year.
seasons: May–September
Dry season in the Andes: sunny days, cold nights and peak Machu Picchu crowds.
December–April
Rainy season in the mountains (the Inca Trail closes in February), but sunny summer in Lima.
April & October–November
Shoulder months with fewer crowds and mixed weather.

Philippines.label: the Philippines
Philippines.intro: The Philippines has two main seasons: a dry season from about December to May and a wet, typhoon-prone season from June to November. Siargao, on the Pacific side, follows a slightly different pattern, with its wettest months from November to February.
seasons: December–February
Cool, dry 'amihan' season: the best time for Boracay and Palawan.
March–May
Hot and dry — peak beach season and calm seas for island hopping.
June–November
Wet season with typhoon risk, especially August–October; prices drop.

Portugal.intro: Portugal is one of Europe's sunniest countries. The mainland is best from spring to autumn, with beach weather on the Algarve from June to September, while Madeira stays mild all year.
seasons: April–June
Warm and sunny with fewer crowds — great for cities and coastal walks.
July–August
Hot, dry and busy: prime beach time on the Algarve.
September–October
Warm sea, grape harvests and quieter beaches.
November–March
Mild but wetter on the mainland; Madeira remains spring-like.

Rocky Mountains.label: the Rocky Mountains
Rocky Mountains.intro: The Rocky Mountains have two great seasons: summer, when high roads like Trail Ridge Road and Going-to-the-Sun Road open and the lakes thaw, and winter, when the ski resorts of Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and Alberta come alive. Spring and late autumn are muddy shoulder seasons with many closures.
seasons: Late June–September
Summer: all roads and trails open, wildflowers in July and golden aspens and larches in September.
December–March
Ski season in Banff, Colorado, Jackson Hole and Park City; most national-park roads are closed.
April–May & October–November
Shoulder seasons: quieter, but with snow, mud and road closures in the high country.

Scandinavia.intro: Scandinavia (and its Nordic neighbour Finland) has two very different travel seasons. Summer brings mild weather and the midnight sun, while winter — dark, snowy and cold — is the season for the northern lights, husky sledding and Christmas in Lapland.
seasons: June–August
Summer: long, light days, midnight sun in the north and the best weather for cities and fjords.
September–March
Northern lights season above the Arctic Circle, best with dark, clear nights.
December–March
Winter: snow, husky and reindeer sledding, and Christmas in Lapland.

Scotland.intro: Scotland's weather is famously changeable, but late spring and summer bring the longest days — up to 18 hours of light — for exploring Edinburgh, the Highlands and Skye.
seasons: May–June
Long days, fewer midges and often the driest weather.
July–August
Warmest months and Edinburgh's festivals, but midges in the Highlands.
November–February
Short, dark days and storms — but cosy pubs and Hogmanay.

South Africa.intro: South Africa's seasons are the reverse of the northern hemisphere's, and its regions differ: Cape Town has dry, sunny summers and wet winters, while safari country around Kruger is best in the dry winter, when animals gather at waterholes.
seasons: November–March
Summer: beach and winelands season in Cape Town; hot and rainy, but green, in Kruger.
May–September
Winter: the best safari season in Kruger; cool and rainy in Cape Town, with whales from June.
April & October
Shoulder months that work well for a combined Cape and safari trip.

South Korea.intro: South Korea has four distinct seasons. Spring brings cherry blossoms and autumn brings brilliant foliage — both ideal for travel — while summer is hot and humid with a monsoon, and winter is cold, dry and good for skiing.
seasons: April–May
Spring: cherry blossoms (early April) and mild, sunny days.
September–November
Autumn: crisp, clear weather and spectacular foliage (mid-October–November).
Late June–August
Monsoon rains and humid heat; beach season in Busan and Jeju.

South Pacific.label: the South Pacific
South Pacific.intro: The South Pacific islands — Fiji, French Polynesia and the Cook Islands — are warm all year. The dry season from May to October brings sunshine, lower humidity and calm lagoons; November to April is hotter and wetter, with cyclone risk.
seasons: May–October
Dry season: sunny, breezy and the most popular time to visit.
November–April
Wet season: hot, humid and showery, with cyclones possible from January to March.
April–May & October–November
Shoulder months with good weather and better rates.

Southeast Asia.intro: Southeast Asia is warm all year, but the monsoons move around the region at different times. Most of mainland Southeast Asia — Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and northern Vietnam — is best from November to March, while Bali and Indonesia are driest from April to October.
seasons: November–March
Dry season on the mainland: Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and most of Vietnam are at their best.
April–October
Dry season in Bali, Lombok and Java; monsoon rains on the Andaman coast of Thailand.
September–December
Rainy and stormy in central Vietnam and on Thailand's Gulf islands (October–December).

Southern Africa.intro: Southern Africa — South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia — is best for safaris in the dry winter, from May to October, when the bush thins out and animals gather at waterholes. The summer rains (November–March) make the landscapes green and bring newborn animals and migrant birds. Cape Town is the exception, with dry, sunny summers and wet winters.
seasons: May–October
Dry season: the best game viewing in Kruger, the Okavango and Namibia; cold mornings.
November–March
Green season: hot afternoons with storms, lush scenery and the best time for Cape Town.
March–May
Victoria Falls at its fullest after the rains.

Spain.intro: Spain has a sunny climate, but it varies widely: Seville and Madrid get very hot in summer, Barcelona and Mallorca are beach destinations from June to September, and the Canary Islands are warm all year.
seasons: April–June
Warm and sunny — the best time for cities like Seville, Madrid and Barcelona.
July–August
Peak beach season; inland cities often top 40°C.
September–October
Warm sea and comfortable temperatures across the country.
November–March
Cool on the mainland; winter sun in the Canary Islands.

Tanzania.intro: Tanzania's safari, mountain and beach seasons line up neatly: the long dry season from June to October is best for the Serengeti, Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar, while January–February brings wildebeest calving on the southern plains.
seasons: June–October
Dry season: prime time for safaris, river crossings, Kilimanjaro climbs and Zanzibar.
January–February
Short dry spell: calving season in the southern Serengeti and good climbing weather.
April–May
Long rains: muddy roads, some camps and hotels close, but lower prices.

Texas.intro: Texas is hot for much of the year, so spring and autumn are the best times for Austin and San Antonio. March to May brings wildflowers and big festivals; summer highs regularly top 35°C; and October to November is warm, sunny and busy with events. Winters are mild, with the odd cold snap.
seasons: March–May
Warm, sunny and green, with bluebonnets and festival season.
June–September
Hot and humid, often above 35°C — best for swimming holes and air-conditioned museums.
October–November
Warm, dry and pleasant, with music festivals and football.

Thailand.intro: Thailand's cool, dry season from November to February is the best time for most of the country. Watch the coasts: the Andaman side (Phuket, Krabi) is wet from May to October, while the Gulf islands (Koh Samui) get their heaviest rain in October to December.
seasons: November–February
Cool, dry season: the best weather in Bangkok, the north and the Andaman coast.
March–May
Hot season — April is the hottest month, and northern Thailand suffers from smoke haze.
June–October
Rainy season on the Andaman coast; Koh Samui stays relatively dry until October.

Türkiye.intro: Türkiye's best seasons are spring and autumn, when Istanbul is pleasant for walking, Cappadocia's balloons fly in calm skies and the Turquoise Coast has warm seas without peak-summer heat.
seasons: April–June
Mild to warm, ideal for Istanbul, Cappadocia and early beach days.
July–August
Hot beach season on the coast; Istanbul is humid and busy.
September–October
Warm sea and comfortable sightseeing weather.
December–February
Cold, wet winters in Istanbul and snow in Cappadocia.

United Kingdom.label: the UK
United Kingdom.intro: The UK’s weather is mild and changeable all year, so the best time to visit is about daylight and crowds. Late spring to early autumn brings long days and festivals; Scotland’s Highlands are best from May to September, and winter is for theatre, museums and Christmas lights.
seasons: May–June
Long days, blooming gardens and fewer crowds than midsummer.
July–August
Warmest weather, school holidays and the Edinburgh festivals — busy and pricier.
November–February
Short, grey days, but Christmas markets, lights, Hogmanay and cosy pubs.

US National Parks.label: the US national parks
US National Parks.intro: America's great national parks have very different seasons. Spring and autumn are best for desert parks like Zion and the Grand Canyon, while Yellowstone and much of Yosemite's high country are only fully open from late spring to autumn.
seasons: April–May
Desert parks at their best; Yosemite's waterfalls peak with snowmelt.
June–August
All roads open in Yellowstone and Yosemite, but hot in the desert and very busy.
September–October
Fewer crowds, comfortable temperatures and autumn colours.
November–March
Many roads close in Yellowstone; the Grand Canyon's South Rim stays open year-round.

Utah.intro: Utah's red-rock national parks bake in summer and can be snowy in winter, so spring and autumn are prime time for hiking. In winter, Utah's dry 'Greatest Snow on Earth' makes Park City one of America's top ski destinations.
seasons: April–May
Spring: ideal hiking temperatures in Zion, Arches and Bryce Canyon.
June–August
Summer: very hot in the desert parks, with monsoon storms in July–August; cool in the mountains.
December–March
Winter: powder skiing in Park City; quiet, sometimes snowy national parks.

Vietnam.intro: Vietnam stretches 1,600 km from north to south, so the weather varies: the south is hot with a dry season from December to April, central Vietnam is best from February to August, and the north has a cool winter and hot, wet summer.
seasons: February–April
The best all-round window: mostly dry and warm across the country.
May–August
Great beach weather in central Vietnam; hot and rainy in Hanoi and Saigon.
September–December
Typhoon and flood season on the central coast; pleasant autumn in Hanoi.
